one_liner: C lexer compiled to Wasm that returns ES module import/export records; 2-3x faster than its own asm.js build.
what_it_does: Lexes JavaScript (and erasable type-only TypeScript in the full build) and returns the list of static imports, dynamic import() calls, import.meta uses and exports with their source offsets, decoded specifiers, import attributes, source/defer phase, typeOnly flags and export origins. The API is `await init(); const [imports, exports, facade, hasModuleSyntax] = parse(source)`; it produces no AST, so callers slice the original string by the returned offsets (for example to rewrite specifiers). Four package exports: full Wasm, full asm.js (CSP-safe), minimal Wasm (v2-shaped records, used by es-module-shims) and minimal asm.js.
how_it_is_fast: A hand-written single-pass C state machine walks the UTF-16 source in Wasm linear memory and tracks only what import/export detection needs (open brace/paren/template stacks, keyword positions), resolving the regex-versus-division ambiguity by backtracking checks against the preceding punctuator instead of building tokens or an AST. The full build adds Wasm SIMD128 scans (i16x8 compares, i8x16 bitmask, count-trailing-zeros) for template literals after 16 scalar templates and for line comments after a 4-character unrolled prefix. On Node the wrapper blits the source into Wasm memory with Buffer.write('utf16le') for sources of 64+ characters, and full-build export records are read straight from memory with a DataView rather than through per-field calls.
when_to_use: Build tools, dev servers and bundler plugins that need every import specifier and its offsets across thousands of modules (dependency graphs, specifier rewriting) at roughly 3-5 ms per MB.
In-browser module analysis where download size matters: the minimal build is about 7.3 KiB Brotli including the inlined Wasm and runs on MVP Wasm engines.
TypeScript sources limited to erasable syntax: the full build reports type-only imports/exports (typeOnly) the way Node type stripping erases them, so one pass handles .js and .ts graphs.
Pages under a CSP that forbids Wasm compilation, via the es-module-lexer/js and es-module-lexer/minimal/js asm.js builds with the same API.
Facade or ESM detection (the third and fourth return values) without a full parse.
when_not_to_use: You need an AST, scopes, validation or code transforms: it is a lexer and accepts some invalid source (README: `export const = 1` yields an empty exports list), so pair it with a real parser such as Acorn or SWC when correctness checking matters.

Non-erasable TypeScript (enum, runtime namespace, parameter properties, legacy decorators) is out of scope, and dynamic import() types in annotation positions are classified heuristically (probablyTypeOnly). JSX support is not documented.
Engines without Wasm SIMD (before Chrome 91, Firefox 89, Safari 16.4) cannot run the full build; use the minimal build, which lacks TypeScript, attributes, facade and export-origin data.
Deeply nested input: more than 1024 open brackets/template substitutions or 512 nested dynamic imports throws a parse error.
Raw scan speed is the only criterion: the catalogued fast-es-module-lexer reports 6.6-18x faster scans than es-module-lexer 1.7.0.

integration.dependencies: none at runtime (single JS file with base64-inlined Wasm; ESM and CJS entry points)
integration.min_toolchain: Node.js 18+; full build needs Wasm SIMD (Chrome 91+, Firefox 89+, Safari 16.4+); minimal build needs ES module support (Chrome 63+, Firefox 67+, Safari 11.1+); rebuilding from source needs Chomp plus emsdk 6.0.0 and fastcomp emsdk 1.40.1
integration.platforms: any JavaScript engine with WebAssembly (SIMD for the full build); asm.js builds for engines or CSP policies without Wasm
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the module holds one Wasm instance and its memory in module-level state and parse() is synchronous, so it is safe within one JS thread, and each worker loads its own instance
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it replaces Acorn only for import/export discovery; it returns offset records, not an AST, and does not validate syntax

gotchas: v3.0.2 (PR #249) made init a function: old `await init` code silently skips compilation and parse() then compiles the Wasm synchronously on first call, which browser main threads restrict. The repo's own bench/index.js still does `if (init) await init;` (last edited in #240, before #249), so with current code the Wasm cold column includes base64 decode plus synchronous WebAssembly compile/instantiate inside the first sample, and the printed module load time understates Wasm load; this biases the cold ratio against Wasm, not for it.

The Wasm-versus-asm.js ratios in the README mix three effects measured only on Node: Wasm versus fastcomp 1.40.1 asm.js codegen, SIMD scans present only in the full Wasm build, and the Node-only Buffer.write source copy in the Wasm wrapper versus a charCodeAt copy loop in the asm.js wrapper; in browsers (no Buffer) the gap is likely smaller (not measured).

Releases before the v3 line pushed onto the fixed 1024-entry open-token stack and 512-entry dynamic-import stack without a depth check, so deeply nested input wrote past the arrays in Wasm memory; PR #243 (merged via #244 into v3) turned that into a parse error. Release 2.2.0 also failed with 'WebAssembly.Memory.grow(): Maximum memory size exceeded' on inputs above about 4 MB (issue #214, broke Vite 8.1.1 builds), fixed in 2.3.0.

Template-literal globs: the README says a literal `*` in the static part of a template specifier is emitted as-is, but decodeTemplate in src/lexer.ts emits it as `\*` to keep the glob invertible; test against the version you ship before treating `specifier` as a pattern.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over fast-es-module-lexer when you need the richer v3 record set (TypeScript typeOnly, import attributes, source/defer phases, export origin analysis, glob specifiers), a CSP-safe asm.js fallback or the dependency already used by es-module-shims and bundler pipelines; fast-es-module-lexer's 6.6-18x lead was measured against 1.7.0, not the 3.x SIMD build. Other wasm-libraries-and-apps siblings (sh-syntax, sax-wasm, markdown-wasm) solve different parsing tasks.
verified_claims_summary: The author's bench/index.js (Node.js 26, unnamed desktop machine, one run per build) lexes the 3.1 MB test/samples set: the full Wasm build takes 4.7 ms/MB cold and 3.2 ms/MB warm versus 14.9 and 6.3 ms/MB for the same C lexer compiled to asm.js by fastcomp emscripten 1.40.1 (3.2x cold, 2.0x warm, derived from page data), and the minimal Wasm build 4.5/3.1 versus 10.8/5.7 ms/MB for minimal asm.js. No Acorn or other JavaScript lexer is in the benchmark; the 'Angular 1 in 1 ms versus over 100 ms for Acorn' line is README prose comparing a lexer with a full parser.
status_note: Actively maintained (v3.0.3 on 2026-10-05, perf commit on 2026-10-06, 2 open issues), MIT, zero runtime dependencies and easy to adopt; the benchmark harness is stale against the v3 init API (wasm cold numbers include synchronous compile) and the only baseline is the project's own asm.js build after the pure-JS port was removed in #204.
